questions.ask: When is our Form ADV annual amendment due, and when do the brochures have to reach clients?
questions.reply: Our fiscal year ends December 31. The annual updating amendment is due within 90 days, so by March 31, and the brochure or a summary of material changes goes to every client within 120 days, by April 30. The section from the compliance calendar is in the panel.
questions.before: Compiling the data for the annual Form ADV update is a recurring operations job, and the dates live in the compliance calendar.
questions.now: The dates come straight from the firm's own compliance calendar, with the section shown. The filing stays with the people responsible for it.

result.query: form adv annual updating amendment brochure deliver days

results.heading: Form ADV annual updating amendment and brochure delivery
results.text:
## Form ADV annual updating amendment and brochure delivery

The annual updating amendment to Form ADV is due within 90 days of our fiscal year end, so by March 31. Operations compiles the data for it during the first quarter.

Within 120 days of fiscal year end, so by April 30, every client receives the current brochure (Form ADV Part 2A) or a summary of material changes.

results.heading: Annual review of our compliance policies
results.text:
## Annual review of our compliance policies

We review our written compliance policies at least once a year. The review covers any new tool that reads client information, including the assistant and what each seat can see.

results.heading: Before accounts are opened
results.text:
## Before accounts are opened

A new household needs two things before operations opens accounts at the custodian:

- A signed advisory agreement.
- Complete account opening forms. The custodian sets these forms. Check that every form is complete before it goes to the custodian, because incomplete forms slow onboarding down.

Request a statement for every outside asset the household wants included in reporting.

questions.ask: What has the assistant been asked today, by whom, and what did it look at?

questions.before: An incident review or the annual compliance review would have to piece together what a new tool could reach and what it read.
questions.now: Every question, the seat that asked it and the systems it looked at are on one record the firm can review.

questions.ask: A client texted my cell about a distribution. Can I just text back?
questions.reply: Business messages by text, chat or personal email are records the firm must keep, on firm or personal devices alike. The policy asks you to answer through the firm's own email or client portal so the archive captures it. The section is in the panel.
questions.before: Many firms have never written their processes down, so the answer depended on who you asked.
questions.now: The answer comes from the firm's own written policy, with the section shown.

result.query: texts chat personal email phone business messages keep

results.heading: Texts, chat and personal email
results.text:
## Texts, chat and personal email

Business messages sent by text, chat or personal email are records too, whether on a firm device or a personal one. Do not answer clients about their accounts by text from your own phone. Reply through the firm's email or the client portal so the archive keeps the message.

results.heading: After the meeting
results.text:
## After the meeting

Meeting note tools can misread action items, so check the notes against what was agreed. Log each follow-up as a task with an owner and a due date. Draft the client email listing the follow-ups and send it to the lead advisor for review. Once approved, it goes out from the firm's own email.

results.heading: What we keep
results.text:
## What we keep

Under the books and records rule we keep, among other things: written communications about recommendations, the movement of funds and securities, and placing orders; client agreements; discretionary authority and powers of attorney; and advertisements.

Dear Grace and Daniel,

Thank you for meeting with us on Friday for your annual review. Here is what we agreed to follow up on:

- Tobias will confirm your cash needs for next quarter by November 24.
- Joanna will collect the statement for your outside account by December 1.
- We will send you a summary of your updated plan by December 4.

If anything changes before then, reply to this email or call the office.

Best regards,
Dana Whitcombe
